newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Suicide bomber kills senior Sri Lanka commando.
newsitem.headline: Suicide bomber kills senior Sri Lanka commando.

text.p: A Tamil Tiger suicide bomber killed a senior Sri Lankan police commando in the country's east on Tuesday, police said.
In a separate attack by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam in the east, seven soldiers bathing in a lake were killed by a landmine blast, military officials said.
"A suicide bomber on a motorcycle rammed into Senior Superintendent of Police Upali Sahabandu's vehicle," a senior officer told Reuters.
"He's dead," the officer said, referring to Sahabandu, a member of the Special Task Force (STF) police commandos.
The LTTE suicide bomber also died in the attack, which occurred in the late afternoon just north of Karativu town, police said. Sahabandu's driver was wounded in the blast, they said.
State radio said Sahabandu was the deputy chief of the STF in eastern Batticaloa, part of the rebels' wouldbe homeland.
Karativu, in Amparai district on the east coast, is about 240 km (150 miles) from the capital Colombo.
The STF is an elite police unit fighting the rebels in the Batticaloa and neighbouring Amparai districts.
Military officials said the seven soldiers died when they were bathing in an irrigation lake and stepped on a mine laid underwater.
The incident occurred in Weli Oya, 240 km (150 miles) northeast of Colombo. No further details were available.

The Tigers overran an STF camp at Pulukunava, also in Amparai district, last Wednesday, killing 36 security personnel and two civilian helpers and wounding 37. It was the Tigers' biggest attack on government forces in more than two months.
Rebel radio monitored by the army indicated 34 guerrillas died in the attack, the military said.
The military launched an offensive against guerrilla jungle bases shortly after the attack, destroying several abandoned rebel camps.
A rebel jungle base in the eastern Pulukunava area came under air and artillery attacks on Tuesday, military officials said, adding that there was no immediate word on guerrilla casualties.
The LTTE were not immediately available for comment.
Troops hunting Tiger guerrillas in the area found a coffin factory when they raided an abandoned rebel base on Monday, a military spokesman said on Tuesday.
The Tigers are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the predominantly Sinhalese island.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The Tigers say the death toll is much higher.
